title: Directly manages 60 people! Why Jensen Huang is unwilling to create a succession plan for NVIDIA

content_html:
According to CNBC, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang recently responded to questions about the company's succession plan at an employee meeting, saying that NVIDIA has a unique business model and therefore does not need a formal succession plan. He believes that establishing a succession mechanism could introduce unnecessary management layers and affect the company's existing flat organizational structure.

NVIDIA currently uses a relatively lean management system, and Huang said he directly manages about 60 employees. According to company regulatory filings, NVIDIA currently has only five executives responsible for running the company: Huang, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, head of worldwide field operations Jay Puri, Executive Vice President of Operations Deborah Shoquist, and Executive Vice President and General Counsel Timothy Teter. Kress once served as acting CEO for 12 days while Huang was on leave.

Huang has also publicly defended this organizational model before, emphasizing that corporate structure should be designed around products and actual output, rather than copying the hierarchical systems of traditional large companies. However, succession remains an important governance risk facing NVIDIA. The report noted that after management changes at the company, Huang's refusal to formulate a formal succession plan may continue to draw attention from the board and investors to the stability of the company's long-term leadership.
